draft.subject: Re: Question about the Firmware Engineer role at WindBorne
draft.body:
I wanted to follow up on my note from a couple weeks back about the Firmware Engineer opening at WindBorne. I know things get busy, so no worries if it got buried.

What pulled me toward WindBorne specifically is the hardware problem sitting underneath the mission. Building firmware for a balloon that has to keep working for weeks in conditions well outside its parts spec, with no way to walk over and reset it, is a different kind of hard than most firmware roles, and that is exactly the kind of constraint I want to be working against. The fact that the data feeds directly into forecasts that agencies like NOAA actually rely on makes the firmware decisions feel like they matter past a demo.

I would still love to hear a bit about what the day to day firmware work there actually looks like, whenever you have a few minutes to spare. Thanks again for your time.
draft.hook_used: Follow-up bump with added genuine motivation tied to WindBorne hardware constraints (extreme cold, unattended field ops) and NOAA data use
